title: The Crucible of Gael
type: Cooperative training arena · Tower of Gael
dek: Huoth’s answer to adventurers who are not yet ready for Wrath: learn strength, flexibility, wisdom and cooperation together.

facts.Location: Pinnacle of the Tower of Gael
facts.Account: Huoth credits Cala’s idea and Nuru’s magic

sources: GAEL_RP.md · Crucible introduction and arena rules, July 2024
body:
The Crucible is a training arena at the pinnacle of the Tower of Gael. Huoth introduces it to adventurers preparing to face Wrath. He acknowledges their courage and strength while warning that they remain far below the power of a Knight of Death.

Preparation through cooperation

Huoth credits Cala with the idea and Nuru with the magic and guile used to establish the arena. In his account, preparation requires strength and judgment: participants must become strong, flexible and wise, and above all learn to work with others.

“Most importantly though, you must learn to work with others.”
Huoth

Teams and champions

The arena’s preserved format pits teams against one another with support from selected Tower guards. The winning team then faces a champion controlled by its opponents. Cooperation, recovery of fallen teammates, positioning and adaptation are built into the exercise. These are the training arrangements in the recovered record, rather than laws governing every battle elsewhere.

A refuge that prepares people to leave

The Tower shelters people but cannot undertake the expedition for them. The Crucible joins its rooms, research and counsel as another way of making dangerous work possible beyond the sanctuary. Gael’s history gives those exercises their purpose: defeating Wrath matters because people must then preserve and rebuild the land.

The open record

The July 2024 introduction establishes the arena’s purpose and location, and the March 2026 session supplies a later example of its use. Its full construction history, complete exercise roster and current schedule remain incomplete. No particular practice session is established as the cause of Wrath’s defeat.

Training above the refuge

The arena’s height and walls shape its exercises. Participants can seek cover, but the barriers also cut off their view of one another. Storm conditions limit the space above them. The format gives each fighter a Tower ally, so learning to direct help is part of learning to fight.

These are the recorded training arrangements. They do not establish that a fall, a defeat or divine magic is harmless in the wider world. The protective exercise is meant to prepare people to leave the Tower and make decisions where the consequences are no longer practice.

When an ally becomes difficult to recognize

In the later recorded session, Nymera and Lucido train opposite Nex and Erebus. Their selected allies change the encounter as much as the fighters do. Lucido’s starlight apparition takes possession of Nymera, leaving her aware but unable to make the use of her own abilities that she expected.

The confusion is audible in the exchange. Nymera objects to attacks on Erebus; Lucido reminds her that he is her teammate. Later he welcomes her back and tells her to go for Nex while he deals with the flying radiant opponent. Cover and interrupted sight make the arena a place where being near a companion does not guarantee that each understands the same fight.

Erebus falls early. Possession takes Nymera out of the action again, and Lucido braces as she climbs over a wall and jumps out of the arena. Nex continues, using heated armor and a wall of fire as the remaining contest closes. His irritation at the others’ movement is part of the exchange, alongside the cleverness of those tactics.

A lesson that does not feel like triumph

Nex is left to face the exercise’s final champion. His first response to the earlier round is to look around at the bodies and call it unpleasant. After being raised, he rolls his shoulder and remarks on how fast the divines are. Erebus stands again too, ashamed of a performance in which he feels he landed no blow. Nymera leaves worried.

The closing responses give Huoth’s lesson a cost even in training. A restored fighter can still be humiliated, frustrated or uncertain about the next battle. The session is recorded long after the original preparation for Wrath; its existence shows the arena being used again, without making that particular exercise a cause of the earlier victory.

The Crucible of Gael is also distinct from Bowene’s proposed Crucible of Valor in Fein Uaill. A shared name for testing people does not place the two at the same arena.

A later friendly practice

A later practice brings Scribonia, Minerva, Severina and Thorn into the Crucible with chosen summoned allies. The participants are explicitly told this is training: being defeated removes a combatant from the exercise rather than establishing a permanent death. After the fight, the narrator describes Nuru congratulating the company.

The match and its rulings do not add new deaths to the war or establish every summoned creature as an independent historical figure.
